## Abstract
Wan-Move enhances motion control in video generative models by integrating motion-aware features into latent space, enabling high-quality and scalable video synthesis.
AI-generated summary
We present Wan-Move, a simple and scalable framework that brings [motion control](/papers?q=motion%20control) to [video generative models](/papers?q=video%20generative%20models). Existing motion-controllable methods typically suffer from coarse control granularity and limited scalability, leaving their outputs insufficient for practical use. We narrow this gap by achieving precise and high-quality [motion control](/papers?q=motion%20control). Our core idea is to directly make the original condition features motion-aware for guiding video synthesis. To this end, we first represent object motions with [dense point trajectories](/papers?q=dense%20point%20trajectories), allowing fine-grained control over the scene. We then project these trajectories into [latent space](/papers?q=latent%20space) and propagate the first frame's features along each trajectory, producing an aligned [spatiotemporal feature map](/papers?q=spatiotemporal%20feature%20map) that tells how each scene element should move. This feature map serves as the updated latent condition, which is naturally integrated into the off-the-shelf [image-to-video model](/papers?q=image-to-video%20model), e.g., Wan-I2V-14B, as [motion guidance](/papers?q=motion%20guidance) without any architecture change. It removes the need for [auxiliary motion encoders](/papers?q=auxiliary%20motion%20encoders) and makes [fine-tuning](/papers?q=fine-tuning) base models easily scalable. Through scaled training, Wan-Move generates 5-second, 480p videos whose [motion control](/papers?q=motion%20control)lability rivals Kling 1.5 Pro's commercial Motion Brush, as indicated by user studies. To support comprehensive evaluation, we further design [MoveBench](/papers?q=MoveBench), a rigorously curated benchmark featuring diverse content categories and hybrid-verified annotations. It is distinguished by larger data volume, longer video durations, and high-quality [motion annotations](/papers?q=motion%20annotations). Extensive experiments on [MoveBench](/papers?q=MoveBench) and the public dataset consistently show Wan-Move's superior motion quality. Code, models, and benchmark data are made publicly available.

### 1. Wan-Move 요약
*   **주제:** 잠재 궤적 안내(Latent Trajectory Guidance)를 통한 움직임 제어 가능한(Motion-controllable) 비디오 생성.
*   **핵심 아이디어:** 기존의 움직임 제어 방식이 가진 **조악한 제어 정밀도**와 **제한된 확장성** 문제를 해결하기 위해, 객체의 움직임을 **조밀한 점 궤적(dense point trajectories)**으로 표현하고, 이를 잠재 공간(latent space)에 투영하여 첫 프레임의 특징(feature)을 궤적을 따라 전파시킵니다.
*   **결과:** 이 과정으로 생성된 **정렬된 시공간 특징 맵(aligned spatiotemporal feature map)**이 기존의 이미지-투-비디오(Image-to-Video) 모델(예: Wan-I2V-14B)에 **움직임 안내(motion guidance)**로 통합되어 아키텍처 변경 없이 정밀하고 고품질의 비디오를 생성합니다.
*   **장점:** 보조 움직임 인코더(auxiliary motion encoders)가 필요 없고, 기본 모델의 미세 조정(fine-tuning)이 쉽고 확장 가능합니다.
*   **성능:** 대규모 훈련을 통해 5초, 480p 비디오를 생성하며, 사용자 연구 결과 상업용 제품인 Kling 1.5 Pro의 Motion Brush와 견줄만한 움직임 제어 능력을 보여줍니다.
*   **벤치마크:** 포괄적인 평가를 위해 다양하고 긴 비디오 및 고품질 움직임 주석을 포함하는 **MoveBench**라는 새로운 벤치마크를 설계했습니다.

[Neural rendering](/papers?q=Neural%20rendering), particularly [3D Gaussian Splatting](/papers?q=3D%20Gaussian%20Splatting) ([3DGS](/papers?q=3DGS)), has evolved rapidly and become a key component for building world models. However, existing viewer solutions remain fragmented, heavy, or constrained by legacy pipelines, resulting in high deployment friction and limited support for dynamic content and generative models. In this work, we present Visionary, an open, web-native platform for real-time various Gaussian Splatting and meshes rendering. Built on an efficient [WebGPU](/papers?q=WebGPU) renderer with per-frame [ONNX inference](/papers?q=ONNX%20inference), Visionary enables dynamic neural processing while maintaining a lightweight, "click-to-run" browser experience.
